subject.title: feat(gateway): add context engine control API

question: Should OpenClaw core accept a generic Gateway context-engine control API and optional ContextEngine control contract now, or should this stay out of core until the API/security boundary is explicitly designed?
rationale: The patch adds a new public control plane and plugin API surface; code review can identify defects, but only maintainers can decide whether this API belongs in core and what compatibility/security contract it should create.

options.title: Sponsor after repairs
options.body: Accept the generic core direction after fixing the advertised-method bug, resolving conflicts, and adding owner-approved docs/tests for the API and scope boundary.

options.title: Narrow or defer
options.body: Ask the contributor to move this to a plugin/downstream integration or a narrower design issue until a missing core extension API is agreed.

options.title: Close direction for now
options.body: Close this PR if maintainers do not want OpenClaw core to expose context-engine maintenance controls through Gateway at this time.

recommendation.title: Sponsor after repairs
recommendation.body: Accept the generic core direction after fixing the advertised-method bug, resolving conflicts, and adding owner-approved docs/tests for the API and scope boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The main unresolved decision is the ContextEngine contract shape, and jalehman has the strongest recent context-engine API ownership signal.
